# 01.software Public Developer Docs

This repository mirrors the external developer documentation for 01.software so
tools such as Context7 can index the public SDK, CLI, and API surface without
access to the private product monorepo.

## Included Docs

- [SDK README](./docs/sdk/README.md)
- [Agent CLI Contract](./docs/cli/agent-cli-contract.md)
- [CLI Exit Codes](./docs/cli/exit-codes.md)

## Context7

Register this public repository in Context7 as the source for 01.software
developer documentation. Context7 indexes this root `README.md` and the
generated `context7.json` limits additional parsing to the `docs` folder in
this mirror.

## Source

These files are generated from an explicit allowlist in the private monorepo.
Do not add internal infrastructure, security, runbook, audit, credential, or
private package documentation to this public mirror.

# Agent CLI Contract

Source: https://github.com/01-office/01-software-docs/blob/main/docs/cli/agent-cli-contract.md

# Agent CLI Contract

The `01 agent` namespace is the machine-stable CLI surface for shell-capable
coding agents. It is separate from the Human CLI (`01 query`, `01 order`, and
other top-level commands), which keeps its existing formatting and exit-code
contract.

## Protocol Version

`01 agent manifest` returns a top-level `version` string. This slice starts at
`"1"`.

Breaking output-shape changes require a version bump. Non-breaking additions,
including new optional fields or operations, stay on the current version.

## Commands

```bash
01 agent manifest [--pretty]
01 agent query <collection> [--where <json>] [--limit <n>] [--page <n>] [--sort <field>] [--select <fields>] [--pretty]
01 agent get <collection> <id> [--select <fields>] [--pretty]
01 agent plan create <collection> (--data-stdin | --data-file <path>) [--pretty]
01 agent plan update <collection> <id> (--data-stdin | --data-file <path>) [--pretty]
01 agent plan delete <collection> <id> [--pretty]
01 agent confirm <planToken> --hash <planHash> [--pretty]
```

Agent mutations accept payload input only through `--data-stdin` or
`--data-file`. The Human CLI `--data <json>` flag is not supported under
`01 agent`.

Human CLI `--dry-run` on top-level `01 create` / `01 update` / `01 delete`
remains a separate, human-facing validation path. It is not the agent write
contract and is unchanged by this slice.

`--limit` and `--page` accept strict positive decimal integers only
(`1`, `2`, `10`, ...). Values such as `0`, `0x10`, `1.5`, or negative numbers
return `INVALID_INPUT`.

## Manifest Shape

```json
{
  "version": "1",
  "collections": {
    "orders": {
      "operations": ["query", "get"],
      "fields": {
        "id": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "createdAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "updatedAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true }
      }
    },
    "products": {
      "operations": ["query", "get"],
      "fields": {
        "id": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "createdAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "updatedAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true }
      }
    },
    "carts": {
      "operations": ["query", "get"],
      "fields": {
        "id": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "createdAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true },
        "updatedAt": { "type": "string", "queryable": true }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

For version `1`, every server-auth collection exposes `query` and `get`.

The first plan/confirm slice additionally advertises `plan:create`,
`plan:update`, and `plan:delete` only on this allowlist:

- `articles`
- `article-categories`
- `article-tags`
- `links`
- `link-categories`
- `link-tags`

All other collections remain read-only through `01 agent` in this slice.

`fields` is advisory discovery metadata. It is not a complete authorization
guarantee; server-side access control remains authoritative. This initial
field set is intentionally conservative and contains only stable document
fields shared across manifest collections.

## Success Output

Default output is compact JSON on stdout:

```json
{
  "id": "ord_123",
  "financialStatus": "paid",
  "displayFinancialStatus": "paid",
  "displayFulfillmentStatus": "unfulfilled",
  "returnStatus": "no_return",
  "primaryDisplayStatus": "paid"
}
```

Passing `--pretty` switches to two-space indented JSON.

`01 agent query <collection>` returns Payload's paginated docs shape:

```json
{
  "docs": [{ "id": "ord_123" }],
  "totalDocs": 42,
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 10,
  "totalPages": 5,
  "hasNextPage": true,
  "hasPrevPage": false
}
```

`01 agent get <collection> <id>` returns the bare document:

```json
{
  "id": "ord_123",
  "orderNumber": "ORD-123",
  "financialStatus": "paid",
  "displayFinancialStatus": "paid",
  "displayFulfillmentStatus": "in_progress",
  "returnStatus": "no_return",
  "primaryDisplayStatus": "preparing",
  "fulfillmentOrders": {
    "docs": [{ "status": "in_progress" }],
    "hasNextPage": false,
    "totalDocs": 1
  },
  "fulfillments": {
    "docs": [],
    "hasNextPage": false,
    "totalDocs": 0
  }
}
```

For ecommerce orders, agents should read the independent axes:
`displayFinancialStatus`, `displayFulfillmentStatus`, `returnStatus`,
`primaryDisplayStatus`, and `returnDisplayStatus`. `status` and
`displayStatus` are deprecated, read-only compatibility aliases during the
migration window; do not use them as the primary order status contract. Use
explicit commerce actions for lifecycle mutations: payment confirmation changes
`financialStatus`, `prepareFulfillmentOrder` moves FulfillmentOrder rows to
`in_progress`, and `createFulfillment` starts shipment. `carrier` and
`trackingNumber` are optional at creation and can be added later with
`updateFulfillment`.

### Plan output

`01 agent plan …` performs validation and discovery only. It does not mutate
remote documents. It writes an expiring local plan file and returns metadata:

```json
{
  "planToken": "eyJwbGFuSWQiOiIuLi4ifQ",
  "planHash": "a1b2…",
  "planId": "6f1d8f2a-…",
  "expiresAt": "2026-05-31T12:15:00.000Z",
  "operation": "create",
  "collection": "articles",
  "confirmCommand": "01 agent confirm eyJwbGFuSWQiOiIuLi4ifQ --hash a1b2…"
}
```

- `planToken` is base64url-encoded JSON containing only `planId`, `planHash`, and
  `expiresAt`. It never contains the mutation payload.
- `confirmCommand` is a copy-paste helper and also excludes raw payload data.

### Confirm output

`01 agent confirm` atomically claims the stored plan, re-checks auth context and
payload hash, rejects stale `updatedAt` for update/delete plans, executes the
mutation, and marks the plan consumed.

```json
{
  "applied": true,
  "operation": "update",
  "collection": "articles",
  "id": "art_123",
  "doc": { "id": "art_123", "title": "Updated" }
}
```

SDK `create` / `update` mutation responses are unwrapped: `doc` is the applied
document without the Payload `{ message, doc }` wrapper. `delete` returns the
removed document in `doc` (SDK `remove` bare document).

## Local plan store

- Default directory: `~/.01software/agent-plans`
- Override: `SOFTWARE_AGENT_PLAN_DIR`
- Plan files are written with mode `0600`; the directory is created `0700` when
  missing.
- Default TTL: 15 minutes from plan creation.
- Plans bind to the current auth/API context fingerprint (publishable key,
  SHA-256 of the secret key, API URL, tenant id). Confirm with different
  credentials returns `PLAN_MISMATCH`.
- `planHash` covers `operation`, `collection`, optional `documentId`, and
  optional `payload`. Confirm recomputes the hash from the stored plan file.
- If the remote mutation fails after claim, the plan returns to `pending` so
  agents can retry confirm with the same token and hash. If the mutation
  succeeds but local finalize fails, the plan stays claimed/consumed and must
  not be re-applied.
- Replay of a claimed or consumed plan returns `PLAN_MISMATCH`.
- Secret-looking field names in mutation payloads are rejected before storage.

## Error Output

Normal errors are JSON on stdout:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_INPUT",
    "message": "Unknown collection \"prodcts\". Did you mean: products?"
  }
}
```

Error codes:

| Code                    | Meaning                                                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `INVALID_INPUT`         | Missing argument, malformed JSON, invalid number, unknown collection, or invalid plan input |
| `AUTH_FAILED`           | Missing, invalid, or expired credentials                                                    |
| `NOT_FOUND`             | Requested resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller                           |
| `INTERNAL`              | Unexpected runtime, network, upstream, or rate-limit failure                                |
| `PLAN_EXPIRED`          | Confirm attempted after plan `expiresAt`                                                    |
| `PLAN_MISMATCH`         | Wrong hash, auth fingerprint, missing plan, or replay of a claimed/consumed plan            |
| `PLAN_STALE`            | Document `updatedAt` changed between plan and confirm for update/delete                     |
| `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` | Collection or operation outside the plan/confirm allowlist                                  |

Exit codes:

| Exit | Error code                                                                              |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success                                                                                 |
| 1    | `INTERNAL`                                                                              |
| 2    | `INVALID_INPUT`, `PLAN_EXPIRED`, `PLAN_MISMATCH`, `PLAN_STALE`, `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION` |
| 3    | `AUTH_FAILED`                                                                           |
| 4    | `NOT_FOUND`                                                                             |

## Side Output Rules

- Stdout contains exactly one JSON value for both success and normal error paths.
- Stderr is reserved for fatal harness failures outside normal command handling.
- No color, spinner, pager, or interactive prompt is used by `01 agent`.
- Missing required input exits immediately with `INVALID_INPUT`.
- `01 agent` reuses existing CLI credentials from environment variables, local
  credentials, or global credentials. It never starts `01 login`.
- Commander help and version output are human-discovery output, not part of the
  machine protocol. Agents should use `01 agent manifest` for JSON discovery.

# CLI Exit Codes

Source: https://github.com/01-office/01-software-docs/blob/main/docs/cli/exit-codes.md

# CLI Exit Codes

Stable shell-script contract for `@01.software/cli`. Exit codes are part of
the public surface — bumping or remapping requires a major version.

## Canonical table

| Code | Meaning                                       | Notes                                                      |
| ---- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | Success                                       | Command completed; no diagnostics on stderr.               |
| 1    | Generic error                                 | Catch-all for unexpected runtime failures.                 |
| 2    | Authentication required / invalid credentials | `01 login` not run, expired token, or invalid `--api-key`. |
| 3    | Validation / invalid arguments                | Bad flag, missing required arg, schema violation.          |
| 4    | Network / upstream failure                    | DNS, TCP, TLS, or non-retryable 5xx from the API.          |
| 5    | Not found (404)                               | Resource does not exist or caller lacks access.            |
| 6    | Rate limited                                  | API returned 429; retry with exponential backoff.          |

## Conventions

- The CLI prints a one-line human-readable error to stderr before exiting
  non-zero. With `--format json`, the same error is also serialized as
  `AdminError` JSON on stdout (see "AdminError shape" below).
- 1 is reserved for "we don't know"; commands SHALL prefer a more specific
  code (2/3/4/5/6) whenever the cause is determinable.
- Composite scripts SHOULD treat any non-zero code as failure unless they
  explicitly handle a specific code (e.g. retrying on `6`).

## AdminError shape (`--format json`)

```json
{
  "type": "validation" | "permission" | "degraded" | "network",
  "code": "<code-literal>",
  "field": "<optional, validation only>",
  "retryAfter": 30,
  "detail": { "message": "..." }
}
```

The exit code maps to the `type` field: `permission → 2`, `validation → 3`,
`network → 4` or `5`, `degraded → 6`.
